done.why: I was told I'd used all 30 turns the session allows, right as I was about to go east from the second Mirror Room to find out whether it was the same room or a twin.

about: The old white house and the caves under it, but with the ground partly caved in and a mirror that shakes the earth when you touch it. You fight your way past a troll and then get into a maze-ish knot of passages around a mirror room that seems to show up in more than one place.

moments.note: The trap door slammed shut and someone barred it behind me. Good jolt, and it told me I'm committed now.
The sword glowing brighter as the troll shows up is a nice bit of warning; the room's bloodstains and axe scratches set the mood fast.
Combat is a dice roll: I swung three times and got knocked down, nicked, and then it was 'ineffective' because I was still recovering. Not much to decide there.
Head comes off, black fog eats the body. Quick, gory, satisfying.
Round Room says passages in all directions but several are caved in, and 'look' doesn't tell me which ones actually go anywhere. I had to guess.
Touching the mirror made the earth rumble and the room shake, and nothing visibly changed. I wanted to know what I'd just done.
West to a Twisting Passage, then north, and I'm in a 'Mirror Room' again that reads identical. Same room or a second one? I was about to test when the turn cap hit.

wished: I wished 'look' in the Round Room told me which passages were actually open instead of just saying several were blocked.
I wished touching the mirror gave me some clue about what the rumble changed, so I could tell if I was being clever or just breaking things.
I wished for a few more turns; 30 ran out right when the mirror rooms got interesting.

lines.line: The trap door crashes shut, and you hear someone barring it.
lines.why: That 'someone' is the first hint there's anyone else down here, and it made the cellar feel like a trap rather than a basement.

lines.line: Bloodstains and deep scratches (perhaps made by an axe) mar the walls.
lines.why: Told me exactly what I was walking into before the troll was even named.

lines.line: It's curtains for the troll as your sword removes his head.
lines.why: The payoff for four turns of bad luck swinging; it reads with a grin.

lines.line: Several of them have unfortunately been blocked by cave-ins.
lines.why: This is where I realized the place had been changed and the map I half-expected wasn't going to hold.

lines.line: There is a rumble from deep within the earth and the room shakes.
lines.why: The one moment where I felt like I'd touched something big and didn't understand it, which is the hook that kept me going.

fun.why: The troll fight and the slammed trap door were fun; the mirror shaking was intriguing. But the fight is pure luck and the Round Room made me guess at exits with no feedback.

engagement.why: I got through the house fast and the cellar pulled me in. The caved-in Round Room and the repeating Mirror Room were starting to feel like a puzzle I'd want to poke at, but I never found out what the rumble did, and the cap landed before anything resolved.

difficulty.why: Nothing stopped me outright. The troll took four swings but that was dice, not thinking. The only real resistance was navigation: blocked passages with no listing of what's open, and a room that may or may not be duplicated.

interestingness.why: The changes I hit (cave-ins, a mirror that shakes the earth, possibly two Mirror Rooms) are the interesting part, but in 30 turns I only brushed against them. The house and troll were straightforward.

prose.why: Terse and functional with a few good lines (the trap door, the troll's head, the black fog). The Round Room's 'unfortunately' is a nice dry touch. Most rooms are a sentence or two and don't linger.
